summary: Ryushin Saito works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Saito was attested as a professor at Bukkyo University in 2015 and on the faculty of Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2026.

Ryushin Sudo (1929–2018) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Taisho University. He served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Ryushin Uryuzu (1932–2015) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Ryukoku University from circa 1951 to 1955. He was affiliated with the Tibetan Tripitaka Research Institute in 1962 and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University from around 1970 to 1998.

Ryusho Hikata (1892–1991) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and at Tohoku University, he held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kyushu University, and served as president of Fukuoka Women's University (1960–1964).

Ryuta Kikutani (born 1978) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held appointments at Tohoku University (attested 2015) and Kyoto University (attested 2020), and was attested as an associate professor at Koyasan University in 2026.

Ryutaro Tsuchida (born 1947) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Marburg, supervised by Wilhelm Rau. He served as an assistant at Marburg (1979–1983) and later taught at the University of Tokyo.

Ryutoku Kimura (born 1947), a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Komazawa University. He served as a research assistant at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1973–1980), lectured at Yamaguchi University (1996), and was chief priest at Kaichōji (2003).
Ryuyu Saito works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Saito studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.
Ryuzan Nishimoto (1891–1974) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. In 1916, he studied under Chishu Kitagawa and Chijo Kitagawa.

Ryōmin Akizuki (1921–1999) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1941 to 1944 and held a post at Saitama Medical University from around 1973 to 1987.

Rüdiger Schmitt (born 1939) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Karl Hoffmann around 1958 to 1965 and held a post at Saarland University from circa 1972 to 2004.
S. A. S. Sarma works in the field of Indology and has held posts at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, attested in 2004 and 2024.
S. Bhaskaran Nair worked in Indology and held posts at the Vishveshvaranand Vedic Research Institute, serving as General Editor (attested 1944, 1992) and Deputy Director (attested 1974–1977, 1986).

S. D. Laddu (1926–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He was affiliated with Savitribai Phule Pune University in 1968 and served as editor of the Annals at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute in 2003.
S. Ghosh worked in Tibetology, serving as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology, both attested in 1982.
S. K. Maity (born 1921) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham around 1950–1953 and held a post at Jadavpur University from circa 1958 to 1986.

S. K. Ramanatha Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Junior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras until 1938 and held a temporary post at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar (1871–1946) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Madras, he lectured at Bengaluru City University (1899–1909) and held the Chair of Indian History and Archæology at the University of Madras (1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri (1880–1943) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at St. Peter's College and the University of Madras. He served as Principal of Madras Sanskrit College, Professor at Presidency College, and Honorary Professor at Annamalai University.

S. M. Natesa Sastri (1859–1906) was an Indologist who studied at Government Arts College, Kumbakonam, and the University of Madras. From circa 1884 to 1888, he worked as an assistant to Robert Sewell at the Archaeological Survey of India.
